issues.title: Quota exhaustion is misclassified in three places, so a 429 burns nineteen operator rounds instead of stopping the run
issues.evidence: src/runtime/modelGateway.ts:498-506 sets errorMessage to "bounded model process did not succeed" on non-zero exit, discarding the provider envelope text; src/app/compilerApplicationPort.ts:1553 classifies section retries by error CODE only (TRANSIENT_PROCESS_FAILURE_CODE), so isUnretryableProviderMessage never sees the text; the driver's PROVIDER BLOCK grep reads bn-r*.log, which never carries it. Phase A §6: weekly 429 on 2026-08-28, nineteen rounds in ~10 minutes, 641 attempts in the revision-6 run.
issues.fix: Preserve the provider envelope text on non-zero exit in the gateway; have the compiler section loop consult isUnretryableProviderMessage on the preserved text, not the code; point the driver's PROVIDER BLOCK grep at attempts.jsonl. All three, or the burn recurs (Phase A adversarial: fixing the loop alone is insufficient).

issues.title: The prompt-length pins are measured on a fixture with no scars and no voice card, so they bound nothing real
issues.evidence: tests/contract-refactor.test.ts:196 and :238 render bookId "money-book" with voiceCard("money-book") and loadBookScars("money-book"); neither exists in config/author-voice-profiles.json (59 profiles) nor config/book-scars/ (5 books), so both render "" and the 62%/76% bounds omit the two largest production blocks. PRE_REFACTOR_CHARS["learning-pack"] = 53312 (:40-45). Franklin's scar file renders ~18.4k chars (37 prohibitions = 15,649; 6 notes = 2,555). The scar file's own _comment records a real 2026-08-08 overflow the suite could not see.
issues.fix: Add a third length test that renders the largest shipped scar file's book with a synthetic voice card and pins that total; then set the real budget. This is the binding constraint on every prompt fix in waves 0-1 — sequence it first.

issues.title: voiceCard is hardcoded null on the candidate route, so no writer prompt for any v25 book carries a register instruction
issues.evidence: src/app/researchCandidateApplicationPort.ts:400 `voiceCard: null,` — the sibling bookScars null was repaired with the comment "This was hardcoded null, which made the ENTIRE scar mechanism inert in production" (:401-408). src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:321 `if (!card) return "";` omits the whole VOICE CARD block. issues.fix: Thread voiceCard(bookId) into the seed, with the bibliography's authorVoice as fallback (R-004). Ship with R-007 so the register templates do not instruct first person the moment they start firing.

issues.title: The book's real author-voice block is already inside the writer prompt, unlabelled, and the contract countermands it
issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-bibliography.ts:46-50 produces authorVoice {register, signatureMoves, avoidMoves}, validated at :261-270, written to toc.json (src/researcher.ts:933) and to source-freeze/book-source.md (:960-964), which rides into the prompt as a source_N record (src/app/compilerApplicationPort.ts:1527-1530). issues.title: "Short sentences, plain verbs" is hardcoded at four sites, one of them unconditional, and outweighs any voice card
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:72 states it unconditionally inside universalCore; :59 and :60 repeat it as the no-card fallback; :325 repeats it in voiceCardSection — the one site that fires only WHEN a card exists, so it contradicts the card it just introduced. src/lib/voiceCard.ts:88-94 philosopher-historian mandates "longer cadence", "measured sentences that can breathe" (6 of 59 profiles). issues.title: The 120-word voice-card budget breaks on overflow, silently discarding the catalog-wide plainness floor that is emitted last
issues.evidence: src/lib/voiceCard.ts:43 WORD_BUDGET = 120; withGuard (:57-67) seeds the total with the 19-word guard and uses `break` at :62, so the first over-budget line drops itself and every later line. src/lib/voiceBible.ts:150-167 emits voice / do / never / sounds-like / always, with the 45-word plainness floor appended last at :165-167 under a comment claiming "every fanout prompt carries it".

issues.title: Register templates instruct a person and cadence the product cannot use — memoirist says first-person, which SEC7 blocks
issues.evidence: src/lib/voiceCard.ts:109-115 memoirist (6 of 59 profiles): "intimate, reflective register; first-person; medium cadence" / "speak from lived experience". issues.fix: Rewrite each template's person field as a rendering instruction: memoirist -> "third-person but close in, the way a memoir's confidences read when retold". Data-only change in REGISTER_TEMPLATES. Must ship with R-003, not after it — wiring the card is what makes this fire.

issues.title: Scar notes — including fact pins and cadence rules — render under an OVER-USE quota header that inverts them
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:246 pushes every scars.notes entry into the over-use list, and :249 heads that list "KNOWN OVER-USED MATERIAL FOR THIS BOOK — each item may appear in at most one teaching unit book-wide; paraphrase the mechanism everywhere else." src/lib/bookScars.ts:41-52 states the inversion explicitly: "That is right for scar tissue and exactly inverted for a prohibition: it would instruct the model to restate an unsafe line in other words." Franklin's "name Franklin early", "no verbatim reprise" and "vary sentence length" notes are all rendered this way.
issues.fix: Render notes under their own no-quota header ("BOOK NOTES — always in force"); keep phrases and frames under the over-use quota.

issues.title: Four contract lines claim "the validator enforces this" for dealt fields no gate reads
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:126 (sceneFrame/requiredBeat), :135 (promptShape/answerStyle/distractorTrap/caseCueIds), :137 (frontShape/retrievalTarget/backShape), :146 (practiceForm/practiceConstraint/ifThenPlanShapes) all end "the validator enforces this". grep -a over src/sections/sectionGate.ts finds sceneFrame only inside advisory message strings (:1617, :1644), requiredBeat nowhere, and zero hits for the others; practiceForm appears only at :1698, also a message string. issues.title: The contract's most-protected style exemplar uses a phrase the same prompt bans

A writer following the method at :139 to the stated bound lands on the blocking comparator.

issues.title: CHOICE PARITY counts words only, and its "move overflow into the explanation" instruction mints the disclaiming explanation
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:139: "write the two distractors FIRST (15-22 words each), then write the key to the longer distractor's word count (±3), moving overflow into the explanation; count words per choice". issues.title: SEC114's opener-saturation gate needs 4 chapters to fire, so a 4-chapter book must be 100% uniform before it blocks
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:1769 `if (chapters.size < ACTION_CHALLENGE_OPENER_MIN_CHAPTERS) continue;` with the constant = 4 at :179, mirrored as maxKeptChapters: 3 in src/app/compilerApplicationPort.ts:656-661; the sibling check on the same pack fires at 2 (:1742, maxKeptChapters: 1 at :650-655). This REFUTES Phase A's stated mechanism: actionChallengeOpener strips digits (:943), which makes "24 hours" and "twenty-four hours" group together; the threshold, not the digit strip, is the hole.

issues.title: Per-role effort tiers are never applied: review and QC run at high, not xhigh
issues.evidence: src/app/bookRunComposition.ts:375 `const modelRoute = createRouteForRoleRoute(resolveRoleRoute(modelRoutingConfig));` — resolveRoleRoute is called with no role, so the default route is used for every role (verified by reading :373-377). Phase A §6 CONFIRMED this against the attempt records.

issues.title: The per-run research attempt cap is a flat 4096 — 300x any real book, so it bounds nothing

The chapter count IS available after the bibliography returns (src/researcher.ts:262 flattenChapters). A 12-chapter book needs 37.

issues.title: The author-verb guard is a hardcoded sixteen-surname list, so it is a no-op for almost every book including Franklin
issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:77-79 META_VERBS = /\b(clear|kahneman|taleb|housel|tetlock|cialdini|greene|machiavelli|duhigg|eyal|covey|ries|brown|kolb|gladwell|fogg)\s+(argues|says|...)\b/i. issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:553-562 builds allText from focus, coreClaim, centralConcept, keyClaims, namedExamples[].summary/teachesWhat, hardEdge and paraphraseNotes; testableFacts, voiceCues, hardSpecifics, example labels and concept names are all absent. src/critics/sourceCoherence.ts:99-108 (SC4) copies the omission. issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:564-570 and :571-577 both `break` after the first match, with MAX_CHAPTER_RESEARCH_ATTEMPTS = 3 at :171 and the documented live failure at :84-85 ("a live Franklin run that died here 3/3 on 'the author'").

issues.title: stripMetaReferences strips no meta-references, while the research prompt tells the model it does

issues.title: SP11 (a hardSpecific floating free of its case) is dead code — its condition can never be true
issues.evidence: src/compiler/sourcePacketGate.ts:66-69 builds supportText as `${c.summary} ${c.hardSpecifics.join(" ")}`.toLowerCase() and then tests whether any specific's first word is missing from it; every specific is inside the join, so the predicate is always false. This is the only packet-level check aimed at a specific floating free of its case — the shape of "rotating duty" and "Leather Apron Club".
issues.fix: Build supportText from c.summary alone (plus paraphraseNotes if threaded); keep the advisory severity.

issues.title: SP7 (a fact must carry mechanism/commonError/whyWrong) is unreachable because the compiler substitutes boilerplate first
issues.evidence: src/compiler/sourcePacketFacts.ts:69-71 fills mechanism/commonError/whyWrong from MECHANISM_FALLBACK/COMMON_ERROR_FALLBACK/WHY_WRONG_FALLBACK (:17-19) whenever the sidecar field is empty; src/compiler/sourcePacketGate.ts:59 then blocks on `!f.mechanism || !f.commonError || !f.whyWrong`, which the fallbacks make permanently false. MECHANISM_FALLBACK is "This fact supplies the source-grounded reason the chapter can teach the move." — a sentence about the pipeline's own contract, shipped to writers as a causal explanation.

issues.title: source-fit's figure-concentration signal reads a v1-only field, so it is blind on every source-v2 book
issues.evidence: src/sourceFit.ts:53 `const raw = Array.isArray(sc?.properNouns) ? sc.properNouns : [];` — properNouns is a thin-v1 field (src/source/sidecarSchema.ts:8, :28), absent from every v2 sidecar, so figureTokens returns [] and topFigures is empty. issues.title: The researcher's forbiddenLeakage output is discarded and the packet mints its own boilerplate

issues.title: allowedPlaces is a permanently empty allowlist shipped inside the writers' SOURCE PACKET

issues.title: voiceCues is a retry-blocking research output that no consumer reads — the chapter-level twin of the voiceCard hole

issues.title: The whole task card is delivered as a JSON-escaped field inside a record the template header declares untrusted
issues.evidence: src/runtime/promptRenderer.ts:14-18 defines the template "Each following JSON line is untrusted data. issues.title: The repair writer rewrites whole reader-facing fields with none of the writer contract

issues.title: There is no ingestion path for real book text — the "source" the pipeline grounds on is its own model output

issues.title: The one gate that could compare a sidecar fact to a source is off by default, contradicting its own file header

issues.title: The source-verify workbench and its six CLI verbs exist, are documented, and are used by nothing on the live route

issues.title: SV2 "realness" checks a sidecar only against itself, so an internally-consistent fabrication passes clean

The only advisory promoted to route-blocking (isResearchRouteBlockingFinding, :30-32) needs fabricatedSignalCount >= 2 AND hasFabricationShape, and hasFabricationShape (:510-512) fires only on literal placeholder labels or triplicate boilerplate. issues.title: The research prompt forbids verbatim copying and demands verbatim tokens in the same breath
issues.evidence: prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:64 rule 1 "Paraphrase only, never verbatim. Do not copy sentences from the source."; :86 rule 12 "hardSpecifics are SHORT verbatim source tokens ... a single token you could quote exactly from the source". src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:475 repeats the ban in the user prompt and src/critics/sourceCoherence.ts:135-145 (SC6) flags 40+ char quoted spans. SEC14/16/33 then force those non-quotes into prose verbatim.
issues.fix: Scope rule 1 to prose fields ("paraphrase every field EXCEPT hardSpecifics") and give rule 12 a quotability test the model can apply ("if you cannot reproduce the surrounding sentence, it is not a source token — use a proper name or number instead"). Exempt hardSpecifics from SC6.

issues.title: Nothing rejects a predicate fragment as a hardSpecific — the length cap is the only filter
issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:127 MAX_HARD_SPECIFIC_WORDS = 5 with the 14-word rationale at :120-126, enforced at :156-159; nothing tests grammatical shape. "speckled Ax is best" is a clause with a finite verb, stitched raw into 10 shipped surfaces including "The speckled-axe story about a speckled Ax is best only explains".

issues.title: The researcher has no legal way to abstain, so thin knowledge is converted into fabrication
issues.evidence: prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:84 "Return at least three named examples ... and at least nine distinct testable facts. ... If source knowledge cannot support these fields honestly, fail the task instead of inventing details." There is no failure channel: no confidence/abstain field in ChapterResearchResult (src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:40-60), and the validator hard-requires the same floors (src/source/sourceIntegrity.ts:337, :353; researcher-chapter.ts:511) feeding shortfalls back for up to MAX_CHAPTER_RESEARCH_ATTEMPTS = 3 (:171). Franklin ch04 covers a quarter of a memoir with 10 facts and 4 cases, five of them wrong.
issues.fix: Add an optional insufficientSource {field, why} escape to the schema and to collectChapterResearchProblems: when present, admit the sidecar under the floor and let the packet gate block the book with an accurate message ("research could not honestly reach the floor") instead of the model padding to reach it.

issues.title: Rule 9's ban on naming the author as an actor makes a memoir's protagonist disappear from the research
issues.evidence: prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:80 "No author-surname-verb constructions. Never write 'Clear argues' ... Write the claim directly, attributable to the chapter without naming the author as an actor." Occurrence counts on the released sidecars: ch01 = 1, ch02 = 14, ch03 = 0, ch04 = 18; ch03's paraphraseNotes is fully agentless ("pooling money is proposed"). The shipped ch3 contains zero occurrences of "Franklin". Note the sharpening: voiceCues cannot be the writer-side cause (R-032 — no writer reads them); the sidecar's own agentless facts and cases, which the packet does carry, are what strip the actor.
issues.fix: Scope rule 9 to attribution verbs about the text (argues/claims/notes/writes) and add a memoir carve-out: "when the book is a memoir or first-person account, the author is the SUBJECT — name him as the actor of what he did, never as the speaker of the text." Add a validator warning when a memoir-classified sidecar's cases and facts contain zero occurrences of the bibliography author's surname.

issues.title: The research system prompt is saturated with one other book's content — the leak the retry card was rewritten to remove
issues.evidence: prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:104 renders a full Atomic Habits Ch1 paragraph as the "Good paraphraseNotes" exemplar ("Dave Brailsford and British Cycling are the central anchor: every small element ... tuned half a percent at a time"), plus rule 3's "90 seconds of friction" (:68), rule 5's worked example (:72) and rule 12's "Dave Brailsford"/"1% per day" (:86). src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:87-95 documents exactly this failure mode for the retry card and notes "The section writers were migrated to that mechanism; the researcher never was." Every Franklin paraphraseNotes follows the mold (one template per project, closing practical rule).
issues.fix: Replace the worked example with a schematic skeleton (field shapes with <...> slots, no book content), or rotate two exemplars from structurally different genres so no single register is the default.

issues.title: The packet drops focus, coreClaim, keyClaims, hardEdge and paraphraseNotes — writers never see the chapter's thesis
issues.evidence: src/compiler/sourcePacket.ts:100-121 carries only schemaVersion, ids, sourceHash, facts, namedCases, frameworks, the allowed* lists, forbiddenClaims, forbiddenLeakage and sourceQuality; src/sections/assembleSections.ts:149-152 synthesises PlanningSourceEvidence with chapterSource: null, chapterSidecar: null, bookSource: null. Meanwhile prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:74 says paraphraseNotes "is what the breakdown writer reads" and :72 says hardEdge exists "so downstream quiz writers can craft distractors around it". Live cost: Franklin ch04 keyClaim 7 says the dispute "ends in a limited compromise on assessment method" (near the truth) while fact.08 says "without a decisive outcome for either side" (false) — the packet keeps the false fact and discards the truer claim.

issues.title: hardSpecifics strip the proposition and the downstream verbatim quotas re-attach a false one
issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:127 caps a specific at 5 words, deleting the relation between tokens. The released ch01 arrival case stores ['three puffy rolls','one Dutch dollar','Market Street']; the source says "my whole stock of cash consisted of a Dutch dollar, and about a shilling in copper" and "three-penny worth ... He gave me, accordingly, three great puffy rolls." SEC16 then requires a 14-word line containing two of them, and the only grammatical join is a false predicate — the shipped "just one Dutch dollar. He spent it on three puffy rolls", found on six surfaces.

issues.title: Research is per-chapter and context-free, so cross-chapter sameness is only detectable after every chapter is paid for
issues.evidence: src/agents/researcher-chapter.ts:470-473 passes only a list of prior chapter TITLES; src/researcher.ts:519-523 confirms { bibliography, chapter, priorChapterTitles } is the whole input; the design comment is at researcher-chapter.ts:13. prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:78 nonetheless asks the model to name "concepts from LATER chapters" it has never been shown. The only remedies are post-hoc: SP14 (src/compiler/sourcePacketGate.ts:43-53), whose message is "Re-research this chapter", and SC8 (src/critics/sourceCoherence.ts:157-205).

issues.title: A four-"chapter" bibliography makes the research unit a quarter of a book while every floor is sized for a chapter
issues.evidence: The released chapter-index is four entries titled "Part One".."Part Four". Against that, prompts/researcher-chapter.system.md:34-53 asks for ONE centralConcept, 4-8 keyClaims, 3-5 namedExamples and >=9 testableFacts, and src/source/sourceIntegrity.ts:337/:353 enforces the same floors. Franklin ch03 covers the Junto, the Library, the fire company, the militia, the hospital, the academy and street paving in 10 facts and 5 cases — the direct cause of the blur and of the omissions the readers scored as the weakest limits factor.
issues.fix: For books whose canonical divisions are Parts, have the bibliography emit sub-divisions (or a chapterCount override) so a research unit is roughly one teachable episode; failing that, raise per-unit floors proportionally for multi-chapter units rather than teaching a quarter-book from nine facts.

issues.title: SEC14 demands two verbatim tokens per cited rich anchor per tier, and fires nothing on the hook and keyTakeaway
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2258 calls validateAnchorHardSpecifics with default min = 2 and default combine = "all" (:260, :275), so every cited specifics-rich anchor must contribute two verbatim strings to each tier; :295 skips anchors with fewer than min specifics. Verified on the live compiler candidate: ch01 deepRead cites 4 rich anchors (8 required) and fullRead cites 5 (10 required), while ch01's hook cites ['ch01.fact.apprenticeship-term'] and its keyTakeaway ['ch01.concept.raw-industry'] — both specifics-free, so SEC14 fires zero requirements on the two most-read sentences.
issues.fix: Make the breakdown call per-CHAPTER (each cited rich anchor grounded once across the three tiers, which the gate already holds in one scope at :2249-2259) and scale min to the unit budget so a short tier never owes eight tokens. This is the single biggest lever on the density and retention factors.

issues.title: SEC16 requires two verbatim tokens inside a <=14-word aphorism, which is why memorable lines are token pairs
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2331 calls validateAnchorHardSpecifics(..., "memorable_line", candidate.text, ..., 2, "any") while SEC118 (:2324) demands <=14-word candidates and memorableLineScore rewards 8-13 words (src/optimizers/memorableLines.ts:180); src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:164-165 states both demands together. The gate's own fix note at :2280-2289 concedes the pressure and relieved only the across-anchor face (OR), not the min. Shipped: "Three puffy rolls and one Dutch dollar bought him a fresh start.", "Forty shillings joined you, ten shillings kept you in."
issues.fix: Drop the memorable-line call to min = 1 — the same P15/F14 reasoning already applied to quiz (:2757) and cards (:2888), where the comment calls the >=2 quota "the MECHANICAL cause of identifier-sentence stuffing". One digit, plus the matching contract wording at sectionTasks.ts:165.

issues.title: SEC33's two-specifics demand reads as a scenario obligation, colliding with the invented-cast rule for a historical source
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:128 "Each example cites a namedExample/example anchor and includes at least two of its hardSpecifics verbatim (SEC33)" with no statement that the fields are pooled; :80-81 requires a NAMED invented person and forbids source figures as props; config/book-scars/the-autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin.json:54 forbids any character recalling or citing Franklin inside the scene. The writer's compromise is Phase A's "remembered the old X" beat (ch3 opens five of six scenarios on a character who "read how the old Library Company got its start"). Note: the gate ALREADY pools fields — src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2473 builds combinedRaw from scenario + whatToDo + whyItMatters and :2480-2484 folds clipped phrases — so this is a prompt-text defect only, not a code one.
issues.fix: State the pooling in the contract: "the two verbatim specifics may live in whatToDo or whyItMatters, not necessarily in the scenario." No code change.

issues.title: Case cues are dealt by position and SEC56 then forces the unrelated case into the stem and explanation
issues.evidence: src/compiler/chapterBlueprint.ts:1054 `caseCueIds: cases.length ? [cases[(n + i - 1) % cases.length]] : []` for quiz and :1068 `[cases[(n * 2 + i) % cases.length]]` for cards, while bestCaseIdForFact is defined at :867 with zero callers (all three verified). src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2759 then validates keyEvidenceIds against `${prompt} ${correctChoice} ${explanation}` at min 1, making the dealt cue mandatory in reader-facing text. Live ch04 q05 cites ch04.case.falmouth-near-wreck on a Penn-negotiation question; the stem opens "A colleague, recalling the near shipwreck off Falmouth as proof Franklin trusted luck over paperwork..." and the explanation disclaims it. src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:181 forbids exactly this staple, so craft and quota point in opposite directions and the quota wins.
issues.fix: Deal caseCueIds with bestCaseIdForFact; make SEC56's keyEvidence call fire only when the keyEvidence anchor is also in sourceAnchorIds, otherwise validate it against the explanation alone (preserving the :2747 fallback to qSourceIds); make the preflight text at :614 conditional to match.

issues.title: SEC39's tie-back overlap is satisfiable by repeating the case's proper nouns, and gets stricter as the researcher writes more
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2495-2503 requires whyItMatters to share stemmed terms with the fact, with `minimum = terms.size >= 12 ? 3 : 2`; factAlignmentTerms (:2208-2216) draws from claim, mechanism, commonError, whyWrong, groundedEntities and groundedNumbers — so restating the entity names satisfies it, and a verbose sidecar raises the demand. Phase A: ch2 ties back 6 of 6 whyItMatters with "the identical premise/gap/terms/principle".
issues.fix: Build factAlignmentTerms from mechanism and whyWrong only, and freeze minimum = 2 regardless of terms.size. Add the contract line that whyItMatters names the case at most once and never as its first clause.

issues.title: Every example slot is required to be a decision scene while the craft brief asks for three non-deliberation scenes
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:82 demands a decision scene in EVERY example; :171 asks for three non-deliberation scenes. The gate behind it, SEC31 (src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2461 with SCENE_DECISION_RE at :102-118), has been widened to include before|after|cost|instead|notices|tries|must|risk|realizes|deadline|fails, and 22 of the 24 shipped scenarios contain none of the strong decision tokens.

issues.title: Book-design deals derived frames and venues from other chapters' tokens, so the variety lever is spent on nonsense
issues.evidence: src/compiler/bookDesign.ts:281, :299, :300 derive frames from cross-chapter material (Phase A: "a first encounter with age twelve" dealt to a ch3 slot), so the writer receives an unusable staging direction and falls back to one skeleton. Phase A flags the false-positive risk: changing this changes designHash and invalidates cached packs.
issues.fix: Restrict derived frames to the chapter's own packet, or drop derivation entirely. Sequence with the wave-4 --regen run since the cache invalidates anyway.

issues.title: Intra-chapter tier restatement is collected then deliberately discarded; the check that does measure it is advisory and fired at 45% and 58%
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:3134-3136 pushes all three tiers per chapter into summaryTierFields and :2121 `if (a.chapterNumber === b.chapterNumber) continue;` throws the intra-chapter pairs away (verified). It IS measured at ship time by src/critics/intraBookFieldSimilarity.ts (BP24 verbatim >=150 chars; B15 content-lemma Jaccard >=0.42 at :67, emitted at :720), wired at src/critics/finalGate.ts:1316/:1325 with severity pinned "minor" at :448. The live repair-r7 QC record carries two B15 WARNs at "share 45%" and "share 58%". Meanwhile src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:118 tells the writer SEC82/SEC83 compare its tiers to each other.
issues.fix: Delete the same-chapter skip for the tier-pair case and emit the existing B15 computation as a SEC-level blocker at >=0.45 for deepRead<->fullRead and fastRead<->deepRead. Do not add another advisory — one exists and was ignored twice on this book. Split the contract sentence at :118 honestly.

issues.title: SEC120 stands down exactly where prose coverage is worst, licensing any detail the tiers never used
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2664-2668 `const anySpecificOnThePage = anchorSpecifics.some(...); if (!anySpecificOnThePage) continue;` — when the summary tiers covered NONE of a cited case's specifics, every quiz and card citing that case may name any of its details freely. The correct blocker was on the SUMMARY pack; it was converted into a licence for the learning pack.
issues.fix: Replace the stand-down with a summary-pack blocker (SEC14b.tier_case_coverage): when a blueprint-dealt rich anchor has zero specifics anywhere in the standalone tiers, block the summary pack rather than waiving SEC120 downstream. Ship with R-010's message fix.

issues.title: SEC52 bans absolutes only in distractors — and waives itself whenever the chapter's own prose uses the trigger
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2778 `if (choiceIndex === q.correctIndex) continue;` exempts the key from STRAWMAN_DISTRACTOR_ABSOLUTE_RE (:70), and :2715-2719 builds proseAbsolutes from the chapter's own tiers with :2796 skipping the blocker whenever the trigger appears there. Measured on the shipped 36 questions: absolutes in 3 keys and 0 of 72 distractors; the "only ... not ..." shape in 7 keys and 0 distractors. Neither SEC53 nor SEC116/121 measures register.
issues.fix: Apply the absolute-trigger rule to all three choices (scoping around the prose carve-out, which otherwise disables the extension too) and add an advisory qualifier-parity counter: flag when a marker appears in the key and in zero distractors on more than a third of a chapter's questions.

issues.title: The transfer floor is satisfied by a metadata string, and bloomsLevel is never checked against the blueprint
issues.evidence: src/metrics/rubricMetrics.ts:331-338 counts a question as transfer when `APPLY.has(bl) || cue` — the bloomsLevel string alone suffices. src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2739 validates bloomsLevel only against the enum while :2744 DOES compare depthLevel to bp.sections.quiz[i].depthLevel. Recomputed on the shipped book: all 36 questions qualify as transfer (floor 6 of 9), 23 of them on the label alone with zero scenario cue. The fresh panel scored quizzes 63 and transfer 71 on the same bytes.
issues.fix: Mirror :2744 for bloomsLevel, and count a question toward SEC117 only when the prompt carries a scenario cue OR the blueprint itself dealt an apply-level slot.

issues.title: The distractor-tell budget permits exactly the 22% rate the rubric it cites forbids, and cannot see the book-wide number
issues.evidence: src/sections/pedagogyThresholds.ts:13 states the goal "distractor tell < 20% book-wide (RUBRIC §3)", :21 concedes "2/9 tells = 22% — just above" it, and :27 sets QUIZ_TELL_MAX_PER_CHAPTER = 2. src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2827-2833 fires SEC116 only above 2 and only as advisory; SEC121 (:2844-2850) blocks only above a majority. Recomputed on the shipped book: tells 2,1,2,3 = 8/36 = 22.2%; only ch04 tripped the advisory, nothing blocked.
issues.fix: Add a book-level blocker at the cross-chapter stage where all chapters are in hand: distractorTellRate(allQuestions) > 20 blocks, naming the offending questionIds. distractorTellRate already exists at src/metrics/rubricMetrics.ts:293 with no caller in the gate. Keep SEC116 as the per-chapter advisory.

issues.title: SEC118 counts clean memorable-line candidates in the harvest pool, not in the three lines that ship
issues.evidence: src/sections/sectionGate.ts:2311-2323 builds cleanMemorableCount over the whole memorableCandidates harvest and :2324 blocks only when that POOL count is under 2; the shipped three are selected separately at :2302, ordered grounded-first then by score, never by cleanliness, and memorableLineScore admits up to 16 words (src/optimizers/memorableLines.ts:165). Shipped word counts: 12,12,11 / 15,25,11 / 9,8,18 / 16,10,30 — 5 of 12 over 14 words, rubric measured 7/12 clean.
issues.fix: Compute cleanMemorableCount over the SELECTED set (one identifier at :2313) and add memorableLineClean as a tiebreak in selectMemorableCandidates. Reword the contract target at sectionTasks.ts:164-166 to say what the writer controls.

issues.title: Tier char floors set a mass target with no novelty requirement and a one-sided ease floor, so restatement is the cheapest fill

issues.title: The section gate contains no accuracy check at all: a keyed answer that contradicts the source passes every check

issues.title: The answer-key judge receives no source context and judges only the index

issues.title: Nothing ever reads a whole chapter as a chapter — four packs are drafted independently and assembled unedited
issues.evidence: Each pack is written from its own slice with no view of the others (src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:579-589), assembled at src/sections/assembleSections.ts and never re-read. The defects that only a whole-chapter reader can see are exactly the ones the panel names: tiers restating each other (R-066), ch1's closing "Judging a sponsor by delivery, not by praise" contradicting its own Keith story two paragraphs up, and the cast collisions in Phase A §2.

issues.title: No book-level promotion gate exists: the panel is a per-chapter defect detector whose score axis decides nothing
issues.evidence: Phase A §5: the seats and the catalog rubric share factor names and weights (src/review/readerReview.ts:93-104 equals compose.py), but seats see only the chapter title (src/review/renderReaderDoc.ts:47-79), are denied factual authority (readerExperienceReview.ts:78), and their 36 escalation WARNs on r7 have no consumer; across 32 scored Franklin reviews the composite stayed within 75.4-79.3 while blockers swung 0 to 7 and BELOW_FLOOR never fired. The fresh six-reader panel scored the same bytes 12 points lower than the handoff card.
issues.fix: Add the book-score instrument as a separate, additive, book-level promotion gate bound to the candidate's manifestDigest, with a split vote failing closed until adjudicated against a cited source and a majority blind-key disagreement becoming a BLOCKER. Pin the reader model and route and never re-roll unchanged bytes. Keep the 70 floor, union-any-seat blockers, median-not-mean and key isolation unchanged. Reserve >=85 as the badge, not the gate, unless the owner accepts ~4% catalog throughput.

issues.title: Scar 24 pins a false ending — it instructs the writer that the Penn dispute is unresolved
issues.evidence: config/book-scars/the-autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin.json scar 24 is a FACT PIN for ch04: "No resolution is reached; the manuscript breaks off". The source says the opposite: "when Lord Mansfield returned to the Council Chamber, where finally the law was allowed to pass". The shipped chapter reads "The Board of Trade never rules on it" and "No ruling from the Board of Trade ever comes, and the fight is still open". The upstream origin is ch04.fact.09 in the research sidecar (R-024).

issues.title: The eight verified source distortions need fact pins, and their sidecars need correcting first
issues.evidence: Phase A §2 verified eight against Gutenberg #20203: the inverted Penn meeting (q05 keys the false history), the deleted royal assent ("our laws were to be made by our Assemblies, to be presented indeed to the king for his royal assent"), the invented unresolved ending, the fire company's "no dues fund" (source: "The small fines ... apply'd to the purchase of fire-engines"), the paving story (source: the subscription "made the people more willing to submit to a tax"), the inverted hospital order (the Assembly's conditional grant carried the bill), the Dutch dollar ("about a shilling in copper" bought the rolls), and ch04 q03's charter claim. The ch03/ch04 revision-6 sidecars already contain several of these errors verbatim, so scars alone cannot fix them.

issues.title: Franklin's scar file requires an appositive on two surfaces and rations it to one in the same prompt

issues.evidence: config/book-scars/the-autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin.json:18 ("CHRONOLOGY PIN (panel blocker, round 11): the Library Company (1731) predates the Union Fire Company (1736)...") and :19 ("CONSISTENCY PIN (panel blocker, round 11)...") both render through src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:246 under the :249 quota header. src/lib/bookScars.ts:41-52 states the inversion: applying the over-use quota to a prohibition "would instruct the model to restate an unsafe line in other words". The shipped ch3 contains zero occurrences of "Franklin" while ch1/ch2/ch4 have 23/39/48; the chapter reads "So people built these things a different way" and "credit stayed with unnamed friends and subscribers, never with one founder."

issues.title: Wave 4: a fresh --regen Franklin run, promote, release, and re-score with the same reader class

issues.title: ModelResult carries no provider message and no populated retryable flag, so every consumer must regex a prose sentence
issues.evidence: src/runtime/modelResult.ts:3 `export interface ModelResult { readonly attemptId; readonly outcome; readonly output?; readonly error?: PortError; }` — no providerMessage, no retryable. src/runtime/modelErrors.ts:67 `export function modelError(code, message, retryable = false)` — grep of src shows no call site ever passes `true`, so the third parameter is dead. Consumers are reduced to regex-on-prose: modelErrors.ts:37-38, :55-58. VERIFIER PARTIAL: 'Real: modelResult.ts:3-8 has no providerMessage, and no call site passes modelError's third arg true (5 call sites, 0 with `, true`). But the retryable CHANNEL does exist — PortError declares `readonly retryable?: boolean` (contracts/v4Core.ts:17) and ModelResult.error is a PortError; and on the exit-0 path error.message already IS the verbatim provider message (modelGateway.ts:498-499). The defect is that neither is ever populated on the path where a quota error actually arrives, not that the interface lacks a channel.'
issues.fix: Populate the existing channels rather than adding new ones: set `error.retryable = false` via modelError's third arg on the unretryable classification, and set the classified provider text as error.message on the non-zero-exit path. Consumers then test a field, not a sentence.

issues.title: The canary drivers' NON-RETRYABLE STOP heuristic can never fire, because the terminal message always contains its own sentinel
issues.evidence: /Users/radinsoltani/cf-canary/drive-bennett.sh:53 `if ! grep -qE 'COMPILER_SECTION_|COMPILER_ASSEMBLY|REVIEW_FAILED|QC_FAILED|research invalid|REPAIR' "$HOME/cf-canary/bn-r$i.log"; then echo "NON-RETRYABLE STOP"; break; fi`. Every quota round's log ends with `BOOK_RUN_COMPILER_FAILED:COMPILER_SECTION_PROCESS_FAILED:...` (bn-r6.log:12), which matches COMPILER_SECTION_, so the negation is always false. Identical guards at drive-franklin-final.sh:56, drive-franklin-stier.sh:56, drive-franklin-resume.sh:32, drive-franklin-close.sh:26. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'drive-bennett.sh:53 verbatim; bn-r6.log:12 is `BOOK_RUN_COMPILER_FAILED:COMPILER_SECTION_PROCESS_FAILED:learning-pack:after 3 attempts:...`, which matches COMPILER_SECTION_, so the negation is always false.'
issues.fix: Invert the control: stop on an explicit allow-list of retryable terminal reasons parsed from `terminal.reason` in run-state/.../run.json (a JSON field, not a log grep), and treat everything else as a stop. Minimum viable: break when three consecutive rounds end in byte-identical terminal lines.

issues.title: The operator compile-retry loop has no upper bound and mints a durable run directory per round (176 for one book)
issues.evidence: src/app/bookRunApplicationService.ts:831 `for (let operatorAttempt = 1; ; operatorAttempt += 1) {` — no terminating condition; `continue`s past every FAILED slot (:835) and grants the first unused ordinal (:855-865). Live: `ls ~/cf-canary/run-state/books/how-to-live-on-24-hours-a-day/runs/ | wc -l` = 176 directories for one book, including compiler-operator-retry-1..20-run-<hash> families for five base runs. Each grant re-reads every lower ordinal (readRun at :833), so round N costs N run-state reads. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'bookRunApplicationService.ts:831 verbatim, GRANT at :853-865; 176 confirmed.'

issues.title: ExecutionProfile.role — the documented role-threading channel — is rejected by the profile validator's exact-key-count check

A profile carrying `role` has 9 keys and prepareTask (modelGateway.ts:285) turns that into MODEL_PROFILE_INVALID. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'validator is on the live path: executionPolicy.ts:208 calls validateExecutionProfile inside resolve().'

issues.title: createRouteForRoleRoute accepts a role parameter and discards it

The returned claude route (claudeRoute.ts:144-173) carries only the constant CLAUDE_ROUTE_ID and no effort/role, and run.json's definition keys contain no route field. issues.fix: Either use it (stamp `id: `${CLAUDE_ROUTE_ID}:${role ?? 'default'}`` so attempt detail names the role) or delete the parameter. Deleting is smaller and removes a false affordance.

issues.title: An unrecognised effort tier silently degrades to "high" instead of failing closed
issues.evidence: src/runtime/claudeRoute.ts:46-50 `function normalizeEffort(effort: string): ClaudeEffort { return effort === "low" || ... || effort === "max" ? effort : "high"; }` with effortArgs at :65-67 feeding it into argv; the comment at :62-64 states the fail-open intent ('unknown strings degrade to the high tier'). VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'cliQualification.ts:69/74 only prove that the `--effort` token appears in --help text (parseClaudeHelpForFlags, :108-114), never that a tier value is accepted.'

issues.title: Run-state records no model, route or effort provenance — a completed book cannot be reproduced or attributed
issues.evidence: src/app/bookRunComposition.ts:376-380 constructs the gateway with `route: modelRoute` and persists nothing about it. Live run.json (~/cf-canary/run-state/books/how-to-live-on-24-hours-a-day/runs/compiler-operator-retry-20-run-6353d6.../run.json) definition keys are exactly [attemptLimits, bookId, commandId, createdAt, inputCandidate, requiredInventory, requiredStages, runId, schemaVersion, sourceGitSha] — no model, no route id, no effort. attempts.jsonl admission carries {admittedAt, attemptId, bookId, operationId, runId, stageId, staleAt}; terminalDetail (modelGateway.ts:357-381) emits only byte/exit fields. config/model-routing.json is untracked-by-run. VERIFIER CONFIRMED (keys re-read from the live file).
issues.fix: Stamp the resolved routing into the run definition (or the first attempt's detail): route/model/effort plus a sha256 digest of model-routing.json. This is the minimum before any before/after comparison can claim both sides used the same instrument.

issues.title: --source-git-sha is accepted unverified, and the drivers stamp HEAD without checking the tree is clean
issues.evidence: src/cli.ts:441 `const sourceGitSha = flags["source-git-sha"];` and the only validation at :448 is `typeof sourceGitSha !== "string" || sourceGitSha.length === 0` — not even a hex-shape check; passed straight to bookRun.run at :474; same non-check in createCliV25Composition (:211-217). drive-bennett.sh:6 / drive-franklin-final.sh:7 / drive-franklin-stier.sh:7 all do `SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` with no cleanliness check, while the released rev-6 pair exists only as uncommitted working-tree modifications. VERIFIER PARTIAL: mechanism confirmed, but "every driver" is wrong — drive-franklin-resume.sh uses a pre-pinned SHA and only prints live HEAD for contrast (line 13), the safer pattern.
issues.fix: In the drivers: `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] || { echo 'DIRTY TREE — refusing to stamp a false sourceGitSha'; exit 1; }`. In the CLI: reject a sha that is not 40 hex chars and warn on a dirty REPO_ROOT.

issues.title: One 30-minute timeout profile governs every call class, from a 20 KB learning-pack draft to a single reader seat

Every live call class resolves to it anyway: compilerApplicationPort.ts:35, candidateRepairApplicationPort.ts:35, researchCandidateApplicationPort.ts:49, bookRunComposition.ts:390, semanticPanelReviewEvaluator.ts:149, laneOrchestrator.ts:470. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'short profiles do exist (pipeline-read-json-v1, 300_000, executionPolicy.ts:60-64); stale horizon confirmed live: admittedAt 06:42:41.521 → staleAt 07:12:44.521.'

issues.title: The code requires runs to be launched under caffeinate; not one driver does
issues.evidence: src/runtime/executionPolicy.ts:96-98: 'NOTE: none of this helps if the HOST sleeps — node timers freeze and wall-clock stretches arbitrarily — so live runs must be launched under `caffeinate -i`.' `grep -l caffeinate /Users/radinsoltani/cf-canary/*.sh` returns nothing; drive-bennett.sh:13, drive-franklin-final.sh:16/23, drive-franklin-stier.sh:16/23, drive-franklin-resume.sh:17, drive-franklin-close.sh:11 invoke `npx tsx src/cli.ts book-run` bare. `grep -rn caffeinate src/ docs/` finds only that one comment. issues.title: OUTPUT_LIMIT and SPAWN_FAILED are folded into the "transient" class and retried against a deterministic failure
issues.evidence: src/runtime/modelGateway.ts:312-317 mappedOutcome returns FAILED for everything but TIMED_OUT/CANCELLED/CLEANUP_FAILED, and :504 assigns MODEL_PROCESS_FAILED — the exact code compilerApplicationPort.ts:75/1553 treats as a rate-limit blip. issues.title: No cost or token accounting exists anywhere on the V4 route; the envelope's own usage numbers are thrown away
issues.evidence: terminalDetail (src/runtime/modelGateway.ts:357-381) records only gateway/process/exit/stdoutBytes/stderrBytes/truncation flags (+ a stream head on failure). The claude envelope it discards carries `"duration_ms","duration_api_ms","num_turns","total_cost_usd","usage":{input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,...}`; normalizeClaudeStdout (claudeRoute.ts:127-128) returns only record.result. The old accounting is formally retired: src/runtime/legacyRouteInventory.ts:22 lists src/cost-tracker.ts {callModel, writeCostManifest, defaultCostManifestPath} as STABLE_DISABLED with no V4 successor. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'a live attempts.jsonl detail holds duration_ms/usage only inside the truncated stdoutHead of a FAILED attempt, never on success.'
issues.fix: Add an optional extractUsage(stdout) beside classifyStdout in createClaudeRoute and append costUsd/inTok/outTok/cacheReadTok/apiMs to terminalDetail on SUCCESS as well as failure (the detail cap is 8 KiB). Per-call-class cost then computes from run-state with one awk.

issues.title: The claude route does not neutralize user-level config while the policy deliberately preserves HOME — the codex route does the opposite
issues.evidence: src/runtime/claudeRoute.ts:147-149 `const base = ["-p", "--output-format", "json", "--model", model, ...effortArgs(effort)]` plus mode args only — nothing suppresses user settings. executionPolicy.ts:23 keeps HOME/USER/LOGNAME/SHELL in ENV_ALLOWLIST with the Keychain rationale at :16-22. codexRoute.ts:49-56 emits `--ignore-user-config`, `--ignore-rules`, `-c project_doc_max_bytes=0`. VERIFIER CONFIRMED: 'CLAUDE_ROUTE_REQUIRED_FLAGS (cliQualification.ts:69/74) contains no suppression flag, so nothing is even probed for.'

issues.title: ch03 turns the Junto's quarterly essay into a weekly deliverable and keys a quiz on the fabrication

issues.title: ch03 says a lottery bought the cannon; eighteen of them were borrowed from the Governor of New York

issues.title: The indenture-exit scar pins the FALSE account: the source says the old indenture was returned with a full discharge

themes: ACCURACY IS BORN AT RESEARCH, AND NOTHING EVER CHECKS IT. The pipeline never reads the book. The researcher writes a sidecar from memory, that sidecar is saved into a folder called 'source-freeze', and from then on every gate that says 'grounded in source' means only 'consistent with what the model recalled'. The Franklin revision-6 sidecars already contain the errors the book shipped — the inverted Penn meeting, the fire company with no dues fund, the invented unresolved ending — so no downstream fix could ever have caught them. The one apparatus that could compare a fact to a real text exists in full (a workbench, six CLI verbs, a checker, a rubber-stamp detector) and is switched off by a single line that contradicts its own file header. The Autobiography is public domain and free; ingesting it and quote-matching the sidecar against it is the cheapest accuracy win available anywhere in this system. Until that lands, every accuracy gate downstream is theatre, and the eight verified distortions will keep being reproduced faithfully.

THE PROMPT TELLS THE WRITER THINGS THAT ARE NOT TRUE. Four contract lines end 'the validator enforces this' about dealt fields no gate reads. The retry card states a matching rule the gate abandoned months ago, and then tells the writer to open a sentence with the raw research token — which is precisely the seam readers named ('until a speckled Ax is best won out'). One blocker message names a tier its own haystack excludes, so the cheapest repair is to copy fullRead sentences up into deepRead, which is the restatement defect a different check flags. Seventy-six of the eighty-two phrases that fail the draft are never shown to the writer. The live delivery branch silently drops the paragraph that tells the writer a gate exists at all. A writer who discovers that some enforcement claims are false discounts all of them, true ones included — so these are not cosmetic; they are the reason the writer trusts the wrong constraints.

VERBATIM-TOKEN QUOTAS MANUFACTURE BOTH THE SEAMS AND THE SAMENESS. Research is required to emit short 'hard specifics' with a five-word cap, which deletes the relation between them — 'one Dutch dollar' and 'three puffy rolls' arrive as two loose tokens. Six separate gates then demand those tokens verbatim in the tiers, the memorable line, the examples, the quiz prompt AND its explanation, and the cards. The memorable-line rule is the worst case: two mandated proper-noun tokens inside a fourteen-word aphorism leaves no room for a principle, so what ships is a token pair, not a maxim. The quiz version is worse still, because the case is dealt by position rather than relevance, so an unrelated case gets welded into the stem and the explanation then argues against it. One specific ends up hammered eleven to seventeen times per chapter. The fix is not to loosen grounding but to move it: ground once per chapter instead of once per unit, drop the memorable-line quota to one, and deal cases by fact rather than by slot number.

NOBODY GAVE THE BOOK A VOICE, AND FOUR RULES FORBID ONE. The voice card is hardcoded null on the live route, so every writer prompt for every v25 book carried no register instruction. Meanwhile the research stage already computed Franklin's register — plainspoken, letters to his son, 'errata', dry self-aware irony — wrote it to disk, and shipped it into the same prompt as an unlabelled untrusted record the contract tells the writer to ignore. Four separate lines then hardcode a house register ('short sentences, plain verbs'), including one that fires only when a voice card exists, so it contradicts the card in the same breath. The word budget on the card breaks rather than skips on overflow, silently dropping the plainness floor that was appended last. And the research prompt's own rule against naming the author as an actor erased the protagonist from a memoir: chapter three contains the word 'Franklin' zero times. Wiring the card is one line; making it safe means fixing the four register mandates and the memoirist template in the same change.

THE GATES MEASURE BOOKKEEPING, NOT LEARNING — AND A REPAIR ROUND VOIDS THEM. More than half the section gate checks citation hygiene: does the id exist, does it resolve, do N of its literal strings appear. None of that is orthogonal to truth; it is unrelated to it. A key that inverts the historical order passes all of it. The pedagogy checks are similarly nominal: a question counts as 'transfer' because the writer typed a metadata label, the distractor-tell budget permits exactly the twenty-two percent rate the rubric it quotes forbids, and the clean-memorable-line check counts candidates in the harvest pool rather than the three lines that ship. Several checks are structurally dead — one can never be true, one is pre-empted by a boilerplate fallback, seven cannot fire on a four-chapter book at all. Worst, the whole gate runs once at assembly; repair lanes then rewrite the same fields with none of the writer's contract and nothing re-gates, which is how a thirty-word line the selector scores at zero ended up in the shipped package.

NOTHING LOOKS AT THE WHOLE CHAPTER OR THE WHOLE BOOK. Four packs are drafted independently from four narrow slices, and the writer is not even told the chapter title, the book title or the author. Research is per-chapter and context-free, so the same organizing template and the same figure recur by default and are only detected after every chapter is paid for. Intra-chapter tier overlap is collected at the cheap point and thrown away one line before it would be computed; the same measurement exists at the expensive point, fired at forty-five and fifty-eight percent on this very book, and is pinned to advisory so it changed nothing. There is no editor. There is no book-level promotion gate — the blind panel is a per-chapter defect detector whose score axis has never decided anything, and the same rubric read by a different reader class moves twelve points on identical bytes. Waves 2 and 4 exist for this: a whole-chapter editor pass with re-gating, and a book-level rubric gate with a pinned reader model, so before-and-after claims mean something.

SEQUENCING AND THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT. Wave 0 is safe: truth-in-contract edits, dead-code repairs, severity mapping, and the quota misclassification that burned nineteen operator rounds in ten minutes. But almost every wave-0 and wave-1 prompt fix ADDS text to a card whose length pins are measured on a fixture with no scars and no voice card — the real Franklin card is roughly double what the test believes it bounds, and the scar file's own history records a production overflow the suite could not see. So the first task in wave 0 is a length test that renders the largest real scar file with a real voice card; everything else in waves 0-1 is budgeted against that number. Wave 1 changes design (source ingestion, per-chapter grounding, fact-aware case dealing); wave 2 adds the two things that do not exist (a fidelity judge and an editor); wave 3 is Franklin's own content; wave 4 is one live --regen run, scored by the same reader class on both sides. Nothing in waves 1-4 should start before the quota classification fix, or the weekly cap will end the run instead of the run ending.
